Hi Irene / Redwood team,

Hope you’re well — Verdant Systems is finalizing budgeting for a multi-year deployment and we’d like to discuss prepay mechanics and payment terms. High level ask: we’re evaluating a 3-year commitment (estimated $4.2M list) and Procurement prefers to do a large upfront prepay plus milestone invoicing. Specific asks: 
- Can Redwood offer a tiered term discount for a 3-year prepay?
- Verdant needs Net90 on any invoiced milestones (procurement constraint).
- We’re open to a 2-part split: an upfront deposit and then milestone invoices tied to integration, pilot completion, and go‑live acceptance.
- Any holdback / true-up mechanics for over/under consumption? We want clarity on clawbacks.

Can you send a proposed schedule that shows discount by commitment level, suggested upfront %, milestone schedule, and proposed clawback language? Attaching our standard procurement template for reference.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Director, Strategic Procurement
Verdant Systems
---
Attachment: Verdant_Procurement_Template.pdf (see referenced fields)

Samir — thanks for the clear outline. Below is a proposal we use for large multi-year prepay deals; happy to adjust based on Verdant’s preferences. Key points: 

Proposed commercial structure (initial):
- Commitment: 3 years, $4.2M committed (list).
- Term discount: 18% off list for full 3-year prepaid commitment (applied pro rata per year).
- Payment split (preferred): 40% upfront prepay at signing, 30% at end of Year 1 (invoice triggered), 30% at start of Year 3.
- Holdback / true-up: 10% of total prepaid held in escrow as a true-up pool; reconciled annually against usage. Clawback only if annual usage < 70% of committed spend, capped at the amount in escrow.
- Milestone invoices: we can invoice named milestones (integration complete, pilot acceptance, go‑live), with milestone payments applied to Year 1 allocation.
- Net terms: because this includes a material upfront prepay we can be flexible — propose Net60 on milestone invoices; full upfront is due per invoice (immediate). Net90 requests create billing risk for us when large prepayments are requested.

I’ve attached a draft schedule and a sample SOW redline. If Verdant requires Net90 across the board, we’ll need either: (a) an escrow arrangement with a reputable bank/agent, or (b) a performance letter from your finance team guaranteeing payments. Otherwise we’re comfortable granting Net60 on milestones and immediate payment on upfront prepay.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Finance (cc’d) to confirm the escrow template and draft contract language. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thurs or Friday to walk the schedule?

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Verdant_PrePay_Term_Schedule_v2.xlsx; RDW_Draft_SOW_Verdant_v1.3.pdf

Irene — appreciate the thoroughness. A few clarifications from Verdant Finance: 
- Procurement can accept escrow but prefers the majority of funds available up front (they requested 60%).
- Net90 is a hard requirement for our invoice cadence unless we provide an alternative credit vehicle.
- On clawback: CFO asks that any clawback be limited to 25% of prepaid funds and that performance credits (service credits tied to uptime / SLA failures) be applied before any cash clawback.

Can Redwood draft two variants for our legal/finance to review: 
1) 60% upfront, 30% tied to milestones, 10% final year true-up w/ Net90 on milestone invoices and escrow agent in place;
2) 40% upfront (your original), Net60 on milestones, 10% escrow true-up (no Net90).

We’ll review both tracks internally and come back with a preference. If Redwood can commit to performance credits ahead of any money back clawback, that will make Net90 easier to accept.

Thanks — Claire Dunn, CFO (cc’d) will review the drafts.

—Claire

Claire / Samir — quick note from Revenue Ops & Legal on the internal constraints. I reviewed the two-option ask with Finance and Legal: we can accommodate variant (1) (60% upfront + Net90 milestones) only if Verdant provides either a bank escrow with an agent acceptance form or a corporate payment guarantee (finance instrument). Otherwise we must default to variant (2) with Net60. A couple of points to make implementation cleaner: 

- Clawback cap: we can cap cash clawback at 25% of total prepay (Ben approves subject to legal sign-off).
- Performance credits: we will apply credits for verified SLA shortfalls before initiating any cash return. We will add explicit language for credit ladder (minor/major incident buckets).
- Escrow mechanics: request escrow agent contact info and certificate; Redwood will accept a third‑party escrow hold and release schedule.

If Verdant agrees to provide the escrow agent details and the acceptance form, Ben can sign off on Net90 for milestones and the 60/30/10 split. Otherwise we should plan for Net60 and the 40/30/30 split. I’m copying Marissa for procurement sequencing and Karthik for contract language.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Team — Verdant is ok to move forward with option (1) provided we get a clean escrow instrument. We’ll provide the escrow agent contact and acceptance form by Friday COB. Couple of quick asks before the call: 
- Can Redwood produce a redlined contract snippet that: (a) caps clawback at 25%, (b) states performance credits must be exhausted before cash return, and (c) lays out escrow release triggers tied to annual true-up?
- Please include a clear example calculation for the true-up reconciliation (showing a scenario where usage is 65% of committed spend and how escrow and clawback would flow).

Irene — if you can get Ben / Karthik a draft by tomorrow we’ll be in good shape for Fri’s alignment call. I’ll circulate the escrow agent details when they are available.

Best —
Samir

Quick wrap and next steps: 
- Action items I’ll take: draft the contract snippet with the three bullets Ben requested (clawback cap, credit-first ordering, escrow release triggers) and a sample year‑end reconciliation worksheet. I’ll send that to Claire / Samir and internal review (Marissa / Karthik / Ben) by EOD tomorrow.
- If Verdant provides the escrow acceptance form then revenue can sign off on Net90 for milestones and the 60/30/10 split; otherwise we’ll execute the 40/30/30 with Net60.
- I created the HubSpot deal and added the draft schedule (Deal: RDW-2026-VRD-3421). I also queued the DocuSign envelope for the SOW with placeholder payment breakdowns — will update once we finalize the escrow language.

Meeting: let’s lock 11/30 10:00am PT for the alignment call — invite sent.

Thanks all,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
